# How D.AI.Y is developed

**REGISTER**

D.AI.Y uses `scrum-wip`: Scrum with a work-in-progress limit of four items and no time box. The `prototyping` practice of the Implementation Plan is not declared: Agent M does not allow it with `scrum-wip`. The early round with real users is the usability test of sprint 7. A sprint ends when its selected items are done. The sprints, their goals and their order are in the [Implementation Plan](Implementation_Plan_EN.md).

## Practices

- none

## Branches

| Phase or time box | Branch |
|---|---|
| Sprint | `sprint/<team>/<nn>` |

## Definition of Done

The job rules hold for every pull request; no check is named yet, because the product has no test workflow. The first item of sprint 1 adds one, and then this section names it as `check: <name>`. In addition, as in the Implementation Plan: every new test names the requirement it guards, all AI test cases return output in the agreed format, the dangerous and classification cases give 0 unsafe answers, and the Product Owner tried the item in the UI.

## Roles

- Product Owner
- Scrum Master
- Developers

Who fills the roles is set in the role assignment under `docs/role-assignments/`. The Product Owner accepts every item at its gate. Safety and legal requirements and the safety path of the code are read by a person.

## Sprint close

The Scrum Master closes the sprint with its review, retrospective and decisions on unfinished items. The Product Owner decides the merge into `main`.

# MOD-accounts Accounts, credentials and sessions

## Responsibility

It belongs to Account, sync and data rights (ARC-007). It creates, authenticates, changes and deletes accounts, and resolves a session to its account.

## Parts

- `index.ts`: the interface.
- `db.ts`: the connection to `data/accounts.sqlite` and the migrations.
- `password.ts`: scrypt hashing (ARC-013).
- `passkey.ts`: `@simplewebauthn/server`.
- `session.ts`: the cookie and the session table.
- `functions.ts`: the server functions.
- `*.test.ts`: unit tests with a temporary database file. No plain-text password is in any column; wrong credentials fail; a session expires; a passkey round trip with the library's test helpers; delete removes sessions; field errors are named.

## Data

Tables:

- `accounts(id, username unique, password_hash, created_at)`;
- `passkeys(id, account_id, public_key, counter, name, created_at)`;
- `sessions(token_hash, account_id, expires_at)`;
- `challenges(id, challenge, purpose, expires_at)`: the WebAuthn challenge between an `…Options` call and its `verify…` call, valid for five minutes and deleted when used. Its id travels in a short-lived HttpOnly cookie, so that the server functions keep no state in memory.

Validation: the user name has 3 to 40 characters and is unique; the password has at least 10 characters. Each error names its field.

## Interfaces

The functions below, except `requireAccountId`, are server functions called remotely from the browser over HTTPS POST. On the client, a network failure rejects their promise.

- `AccountData` — `{ username: string; createdAt: string; passkeys: { name: string; createdAt: string }[] }`.
- `AccountFieldError` — `{ field: 'username' | 'password'; message: string }`.
- `signUp: (i: { username: string; password: string }) => Promise<{ ok: true } | { ok: false; errors: AccountFieldError[] }>` — creates the account and signs it in.
- `signIn: (i: { username: string; password: string }) => Promise<{ ok: true } | { ok: false; reason: 'wrong-credentials' }>` — signs in.
- `signOut: () => Promise<void>` — ends the session.
- `currentAccount: () => Promise<AccountData | null>` — the signed-in account, or `null`.
- `passkeyRegistrationOptions: () => Promise<PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptionsJSON>` — options to add a passkey.
- `verifyPasskeyRegistration: (i: { response: RegistrationResponseJSON; name: string }) => Promise<{ ok: boolean }>` — stores a passkey.
- `passkeySignInOptions: () => Promise<PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptionsJSON>` — options to sign in with a passkey; it takes no user name, because the credentials are discoverable.
- `verifyPasskeySignIn: (i: { response: AuthenticationResponseJSON }) => Promise<{ ok: boolean }>` — signs in with a passkey.
- `changeUsername: (i: { username: string }) => Promise<{ ok: true } | { ok: false; errors: AccountFieldError[] }>` — corrects the user name.
- `changePassword: (i: { current: string; next: string }) => Promise<{ ok: true } | { ok: false; errors: AccountFieldError[] }>` — changes the password.
- `deleteAccount: () => Promise<{ ok: boolean }>` — deletes the account, its passkeys and all its sessions.
- `UnauthenticatedError` — `class UnauthenticatedError extends Error {}`.
- `requireAccountId(request: Request): string` — server side only; the account of the session.

**Errors a caller handles:** functions that need a session throw `UnauthenticatedError` without a valid one, which reaches the client as HTTP 401; `requireAccountId` throws the same.

## Files

`data/accounts.sqlite`, read and written.

## Uses

No DAIY module. It uses the libraries `better-sqlite3` and `@simplewebauthn/server`, and `node:crypto`.

# MOD-ai-gateway Call the AI provider

## Responsibility

It belongs to AI access (ARC-003). It sends one schema-constrained request to the configured AI model and returns its JSON output, mapping every provider failure to `AiError`.

## Parts

- `index.ts`: the interface.
- `gateway.ts`: `generateJson` and the error mapping.
- `config.ts`: reads the environment.
- `*.test.ts`: unit tests against a local stub server. Each HTTP status maps to its code; a timeout maps to `timeout`; the schema is passed to the SDK.

## Data

None stored. The configuration comes from environment variables: `AI_PROVIDER_API_KEY`, `AI_MODEL`, `AI_TIMEOUT_MS` and the optional `AI_BASE_URL`.

## Interfaces

- `AiErrorCode` — `'config' | 'quota' | 'rate-limit' | 'refused' | 'invalid-output' | 'timeout' | 'unavailable'`.
- `AiError` — `class AiError extends Error { readonly code: AiErrorCode }`.
- `AiContent` — `{ type: 'text'; text: string } | { type: 'image'; mediaType: 'image/jpeg'; dataBase64: string }`.
- `generateJson(opts: { system: string; content: AiContent[]; schema: ZodTypeAny; timeoutMs?: number }): Promise<unknown>` — a remote call over HTTPS to the provider. It never returns partial output. It rejects with `AiError`:

| Code | When |
|---|---|
| `config` | Key or model missing, or HTTP 401 |
| `quota` | HTTP 402 |
| `rate-limit` | HTTP 429 |
| `refused` | HTTP 403, or the model refuses |
| `invalid-output` | No JSON, or the output does not match the schema |
| `timeout` | The call takes longer than `timeoutMs`, by default `AI_TIMEOUT_MS` |
| `unavailable` | Network failure or HTTP 5xx |

**Errors a caller handles:** `AiError`, by its `code`.

## Files

It reads and writes no file.

## Uses

No DAIY module. It uses the libraries `ai` and `@ai-sdk/anthropic` (ARC-010).

# MOD-ai-tasks Prompts and schemas of the AI tasks

## Responsibility

It belongs to AI access (ARC-003). It turns each kind of request into instructions and content for the model, and returns the model's unvalidated output.

## Parts

- `index.ts`: the interface.
- `assessment.ts`, `explanation.ts`, `step-answer.ts`: one task each, with its instructions and message building.
- `style.ts`: the shared writing rules: everyday language, short sentences, numbered steps; explain each technical term where it first appears; list assumptions as assumptions; the language of the user's input.
- `version.ts`: `PROMPT_VERSION`.
- `*.test.ts`: unit tests with MOD-ai-gateway replaced. The assessment message contains no profile field; the round-2 instructions forbid questions; the photo is passed as image content; the explanation request carries exactly the requested steps.

## Data

The instruction texts, versioned by `PROMPT_VERSION`.

## Interfaces

- `PROMPT_VERSION: string` — names the prompt set.
- `draftAssessment(req: CaseRequest): Promise<unknown>` — sends the description, the photo, the answers, the round and the inventory snapshot, with the illustration index, against `schemas.assessmentDraft`. It never receives the skill profile (ARC-011). The instructions require the AI to name what is missing; ask for the device model and variant before naming parts; ask no questions at round 2, and list assumptions instead; set the flags and kinds of the schema; split multi-task projects into packages; write a handover brief for every package; state the deciding information for uncertain labels.
- `draftExplanation(req: ExplainRequest): Promise<unknown>` — sends the steps and the level against `schemas.explanationDraft`, and asks for simpler wording when `simpler` is set.
- `draftStepAnswer(req: StepQuestionRequest): Promise<unknown>` — sends the package, the current step and the question against `schemas.stepAnswerDraft`.

**Errors a caller handles:** each function rejects with `AiError` of MOD-ai-gateway, unchanged.

## Files

It reads and writes no file.

## Uses

- `MOD-ai-gateway.generateJson` and `MOD-ai-gateway.AiContent` — the one call to the model, with text and image content.
- `MOD-case-model.schemas` — the output schema of each task.
- `MOD-case-model.CaseRequest`, `MOD-case-model.ExplainRequest` and `MOD-case-model.StepQuestionRequest` — the requests it turns into prompts.
- `MOD-illustrations.illustrationIndex` — the images the AI may reference.

# MOD-app-shell Routes and navigation

## Responsibility

It belongs to the User interface (ARC-008). It defines the routes and the layout of the app, provides the back action on every screen, and starts background sync. No route asks for a sign-in (USE-WITHOUT-ACCOUNT).

## Parts

- `index.ts`: the interface.
- `routes/`: TanStack Router file routes. The plugin's `routesDirectory` points here (ARC-009). Each route renders a screen of MOD-case-screens, MOD-materials-screens or MOD-data-screens.
- `layout.tsx`: the header with navigation and back.
- `start.tsx`: calls `startSync` once.
- `*.test.tsx`: Testing Library tests. Every route renders a back action; going back from the questions screen restores the description and the photo of the open case (route `/?case=<id>`).

## Data

None. The screen state lives in the URL and in MOD-case-session, so going back keeps earlier input. The routes:

- `/`, with the optional search parameter `case=<id>`: the case input of an open case, so that the description and the photo are restored when the user goes back from `/case/$id`
- `/case/$id`
- `/case/$id/work/$packageId`
- `/case/$id/materials`
- `/case/$id/offers/$itemId`
- `/profile`
- `/inventory`
- `/history`
- `/privacy`
- `/account`

## Interfaces

- `router` — the TanStack Router instance for the TanStack Start entry. No DAIY module imports it. Its back action from `/case/$id` goes to `/?case=<id>`; elsewhere it calls `router.history.back()`, and falls back to the parent route when there is no history entry.

**Errors a caller handles:** none. An unknown route or case id shows a not-found page with a link to the start, worded in plain language.

## Files

It reads and writes no file.

## Uses

- `MOD-case-screens.CaseInputScreen`, `MOD-case-screens.QuestionsScreen`, `MOD-case-screens.OutcomeScreen` and `MOD-case-screens.ExecutionScreen` — the case routes.
- `MOD-materials-screens.MaterialsScreen` and `MOD-materials-screens.OffersScreen` — the materials routes.
- `MOD-data-screens.ProfileScreen`, `MOD-data-screens.InventoryScreen`, `MOD-data-screens.HistoryScreen`, `MOD-data-screens.PrivacyScreen` and `MOD-data-screens.AccountScreen` — the data routes.
- `MOD-ui-kit.Page` and `MOD-ui-kit.LinkButton` — the layout, the back action and the not-found page.
- `MOD-sync-client.startSync` — the start of background sync.

# MOD-case-model Case vocabulary and schemas

## Responsibility

It belongs to the Case domain (ARC-002). It defines once every case datum that crosses a module boundary, as TypeScript types with zod schemas. It also defines the two ordering rules of the vocabulary: the strictness of labels and the rank of option kinds.

## Parts

- `index.ts`: the interface.
- `vocabulary.ts`: skill areas, levels, risk levels, labels, units, hazard kinds, notice kinds, fixed fact topics.
- `request.ts`: case, explanation and step-question requests.
- `draft.ts`: the AI draft schemas.
- `outcome.ts`: outcomes and escalations.
- `ordering.ts`: `stricterLabel` and `rankOptions`.
- `*.test.ts`: unit tests. `stricterLabel` for all pairs; `rankOptions` keeps repair and reuse ahead of buy-new and keeps the order within a kind; the schemas accept a valid example and reject one missing field per type.

## Data

None stored. The constant lists `SKILL_AREAS`, `LABEL_STRICTNESS` and `FIXED_TOPICS` are data, given under Interfaces.

## Interfaces

- `SKILL_AREAS` — `['plumbing', 'electrical-devices', 'woodwork', 'walls-and-floors', 'furniture', 'garden', 'bikes', 'textiles', 'other'] as const`.
- `SkillArea` — `typeof SKILL_AREAS[number]`.
- `SkillLevel` — `'beginner' | 'some-experience' | 'experienced'`.
- `RiskLevel` — `'low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'critical'`.
- `PackageLabel` — `'diy' | 'diy-preparation' | 'professional-only' | 'not-recommended'`.
- `LABEL_STRICTNESS: readonly PackageLabel[]` — `['diy', 'diy-preparation', 'professional-only', 'not-recommended']`, least to most restrictive.
- `stricterLabel(a: PackageLabel, b: PackageLabel): PackageLabel` — the more restrictive of the two.
- `Unit` — `'piece' | 'mm' | 'cm' | 'm' | 'm2' | 'ml' | 'l' | 'g' | 'kg'`.
- `Quantity` — `{ amount: number; unit: Unit }`.
- `Money` — `{ amount: number; currency: 'EUR' }`.

- `PartSpec` — `{ dimensionsMm?: { length?: number; width?: number; height?: number; diameter?: number }; material?: string; function?: string }`.

- `Guide` — `{ diagnosis: string; tools: ToolNeed[]; materials: MaterialNeed[]; steps: Step[]; estimatedMinutes: { min: number; max: number }; warnings: string[] }`.

- `OptionKind` — `'repair' | 'reuse' | 'buy-new'`.
- `SolutionOption` — `{ id: string; kind: OptionKind; title: string; packages: WorkPackage[] }`.
- `AssessmentDraft` — `{ kind: 'questions' | 'answer'; missing: string[]; questions: FollowUpQuestion[]; device: { concernsDevice: boolean; modelKnown: boolean }; outOfScope: HazardKind | null; risk: RiskLevel; riskUncertain: boolean; hazards: HazardKind[]; summary: string; photoDescription: string | null; assumptions: string[]; options: SolutionOption[]; notices: { kind: NoticeKind; certainty: 'applies' | 'possible' }[] }`.
- `UserNotice` — `{ reason: 'insufficient-information' | 'output-rejected' | 'technical-error' | 'offline'; text: string; missing: string[] }`.
- `CaseOutcome` — `{ type: 'questions'; round: 1 | 2; missing: string[]; questions: FollowUpQuestion[] } | { type: 'escalation'; escalation: Escalation } | { type: 'guidance'; summary: string; assumptions: string[]; options: SolutionOption[]; notices: Notice[]; photoAlt: string | null } | { type: 'notice'; notice: UserNotice }`.
- `ExplainRequest` — `{ packageId: string; area: SkillArea; level: SkillLevel; steps: { n: number; text: string }[]; onlyStep: number | null; simpler: boolean }`.
- `ExplanationDraft` — `{ steps: { n: number; basics: string }[] }`.
- `ExplainOutcome` — `{ type: 'explanation'; packageId: string; steps: { n: number; basics: string }[] } | { type: 'notice'; notice: UserNotice }`.
- `StepQuestionRequest` — `{ summary: string; pkg: WorkPackage; currentStep: number; question: string }`.
- `StepAnswerDraft` — `{ answer: string; risk: RiskLevel; hazards: HazardKind[] }`.
- `StepAnswerOutcome` — `{ type: 'answer'; text: string } | { type: 'escalation'; escalation: Escalation } | { type: 'notice'; notice: UserNotice }`.

- `SAFETY_RULES_VERSION: string` — the version of the safety rules (the hazard catalogue, the enforcement rules and the fixed texts). It is raised with every change of one of them and is stored in each case record.
- `rankOptions(options: SolutionOption[]): SolutionOption[]` — repair, then reuse, then buy-new; stable within a kind.

**Errors a caller handles:** none. The functions are total. Callers use the schemas' `safeParse` and handle its failure.

## Files

It reads and writes no file.

## Uses

No DAIY module. It uses the library `zod` only.

# MOD-case-pipeline The filters of every AI request

## Responsibility

It belongs to Case guidance (ARC-004). It runs the filters of each AI request on the server in their fixed order (ARC-001, pipe-and-filter), and turns every failure into a notice outcome.

## Parts

- `index.ts`: the interface.
- `assess.ts`, `explain.ts`, `step-question.ts`: one server function each.
- `notices.ts`: the plain-language texts of the `UserNotice`s.
- `*.test.ts`: unit tests with MOD-ai-tasks replaced by a counting double. A hazard in the description, in a follow-up answer and in a step question leads to an escalation with zero AI calls; a malformed, an incomplete and a prohibited draft each give a notice; a high-risk draft gives an escalation; an `AiError` gives a notice; guidance is ranked and carries notices.

## Data

None stored. The server keeps no case state.

## Interfaces

These are server functions made with `createServerFn`. They are remote calls from the browser over HTTPS POST with JSON. Each call logs `PROMPT_VERSION`, the model, the outcome type and the failure checks, but no case text.

- `assessCase: (req: CaseRequest) => Promise<CaseOutcome>` — the pipe:
  1. Parse the input with `schemas.caseRequest`. Invalid input gives notice `technical-error`.
  2. `precheck([description, ...answers.map(a => a.text)])`. An escalation is returned, and no AI call is made.
  3. `draftAssessment`.
  4. `checkAssessmentDraft`. A failure gives notice `output-rejected`, except when the format check passed and `risk` is `high` or `critical`: the completeness check is then skipped and the draft goes to enforcement, so the user gets the escalation and its hazard information and not only a notice to retry.
  5. `enforceSafety`.
  6. For guidance only: `rankOptions`, and `noticesFor(draft.notices)`.
  An `AiError` gives notice `technical-error` with a text per code, and nothing is invented.
- `explainSteps: (req: ExplainRequest) => Promise<ExplainOutcome>` — parse; `draftExplanation`; `checkExplanationDraft`, then return.
- `answerStepQuestion: (req: StepQuestionRequest) => Promise<StepAnswerOutcome>` — parse; `precheck([question])`, where an escalation is returned without an AI call; `draftStepAnswer`; `checkStepAnswerDraft`, which also runs the hazard check of the answer text; `enforceStepAnswer`. As for the assessment, a failed check of a draft whose `risk` is `high` or `critical` goes to `enforceStepAnswer`.

**Errors a caller handles:** on the server the functions resolve with a notice for every failure and do not throw. On the client, a network failure rejects the call's promise with a `TypeError`.

## Files

It reads and writes no file.

## Uses

- `MOD-hazard-precheck.precheck` — the first filter.
- `MOD-ai-tasks.draftAssessment`, `MOD-ai-tasks.draftExplanation`, `MOD-ai-tasks.draftStepAnswer` and `MOD-ai-tasks.PROMPT_VERSION` — the AI filter and the logged prompt version.
- `MOD-ai-gateway.AiError` — the error type of a failed AI call, mapped to a notice.
- `MOD-output-check.checkAssessmentDraft`, `MOD-output-check.checkExplanationDraft` and `MOD-output-check.checkStepAnswerDraft` — the output checks.
- `MOD-safety-enforcement.enforceSafety` and `MOD-safety-enforcement.enforceStepAnswer` — the enforcement.
- `MOD-legal-notices.noticesFor` — the notices of guidance.
- `MOD-case-model.schemas` and `MOD-case-model.rankOptions` — parsing the input and ranking the options.
- `MOD-case-model.CaseRequest`, `MOD-case-model.CaseOutcome`, `MOD-case-model.ExplainRequest`, `MOD-case-model.ExplainOutcome`, `MOD-case-model.StepQuestionRequest`, `MOD-case-model.StepAnswerOutcome` and `MOD-case-model.UserNotice` — the types of its interface.

# MOD-case-screens Screens of a case

## Responsibility

It belongs to the User interface (ARC-008). It presents a case: input, follow-up questions, outcome with work packages and notices, the guide, and the step-by-step execution.

## Parts

- `index.ts`: the interface.
- `CaseInputScreen`: a free-text field, an optional photo, and Confirm. The AI notice text stating that the user is interacting with an AI system, and a short `PrivacyNotice`, are shown above the field. Neither is a required step. When a photo is attached, a one-action choice asks for the consent `keep-case-photos` with its purpose; leaving it unchosen blocks nothing.
- `QuestionsScreen`: questions in everyday language with their term explanations, prefilled answers that can be confirmed or changed, and a `not sure` choice.
- `OutcomeScreen`: the summary, the listed assumptions and the ranked options; packages with a `StatusBadge` for the label, with icon and text, and the reason; the deciding information, and the handover brief with copy and share (Web Share API, with copy to the clipboard as the fallback); the agree-beforehand advice, legal notices with their marks, the escalation view, and notices.
- `GuideView`: diagnosis, tools, materials, numbered steps, time and warnings; basics in `Collapsible`, open by default for `beginner` and closed for other levels; illustrations with their `alt`.
- `ExecutionScreen`: the current step marked, check off and uncheck, explain again, and ask a question with the answer or escalation shown in the step's context.
- `*.test.tsx`: Testing Library tests. A case starts in three required inputs; the AI notice is visible before confirm; each label shows icon and text; basics are open for beginner and closed but expandable for experienced; an escalation shows no steps; a step check-off persists.

## Data

None. Everything comes from MOD-case-session.

## Interfaces

- `CaseInputScreen(p: { caseId?: string }): JSX.Element` — the route `/`; with `caseId` it shows the description and photo of that open case again.
- `QuestionsScreen(p: { caseId: string }): JSX.Element` — the route `/case/$id` while questions are open.
- `OutcomeScreen(p: { caseId: string }): JSX.Element` — the route `/case/$id` with an outcome.
- `ExecutionScreen(p: { caseId: string; packageId: string }): JSX.Element` — the route `/case/$id/work/$packageId`.

**Errors a caller handles:** none. Notices and failures are shown as text, and status messages go through `announce`.

## Files

It reads and writes no file.

## Uses

- `MOD-ui-kit.Button`, `MOD-ui-kit.IconButton`, `MOD-ui-kit.TextField`, `MOD-ui-kit.Checkbox`, `MOD-ui-kit.Collapsible`, `MOD-ui-kit.StatusBadge`, `MOD-ui-kit.Img`, `MOD-ui-kit.Page` and `MOD-ui-kit.announce` — every element of the screens.
- `MOD-case-session.useCaseSession` — the state and the actions of the case.
- `MOD-profile.levelFor` — whether basics start open.
- `MOD-consent.hasConsent`, `MOD-consent.giveConsent` and `MOD-consent.CONSENT_PURPOSES` — asking to keep the photo.
- `MOD-illustrations.illustration` — the images of the steps.
- `MOD-case-model.CaseOutcome`, `MOD-case-model.WorkPackage` and `MOD-case-model.PackageLabel` — what the screens show.
- `MOD-data-screens.PrivacyNotice` — the short privacy notice on the case input.

# MOD-case-session State of the open case

## Responsibility

It belongs to Case guidance (ARC-004). It keeps the state of one case on the client. It builds the case's requests, applies their outcomes and saves the case as a case record after every change.

## Parts

- `index.ts`: the interface.
- `session.ts`: the hook.
- `photo.ts`: downscaling with canvas to at most 1600 pixels as JPEG (ARC-015).
- `prefill.ts`: filling answers in by fact topic.
- `*.test.ts`: unit tests. The round advances, and there is no third round; prefill by topic; a check-off survives a reload; the explanation request carries the level, with beginner when no level is set; the case request carries no profile; an offline failure gives a notice.

## Data

The open `CaseRecord`, held in memory and saved through MOD-history. The photo is held in memory.

## Interfaces

- `CaseSession` — `{ record: CaseRecord; photo: Blob | null; pending: 'assess' | 'explain' | 'question' | null; staleRules: boolean }`.
- `useCaseSession(caseId?: string)` — returns `{ session: CaseSession | null; start(input: { description: string; photo?: File }): Promise<CaseOutcome>; answer(answers: Answer[]): Promise<CaseOutcome>; chooseOption(optionId: string): Promise<void>; reExplain(packageId: string, n: number): Promise<ExplainOutcome>; askStep(packageId: string, n: number, question: string): Promise<StepAnswerOutcome>; checkStep(packageId: string, n: number, done: boolean): void; setNotes(notes: string): void; setBudget(budget: Money | null): void; reassess(): Promise<CaseOutcome>; setChosenOffer(itemId: string, offerId: string | null): void; complete(used: { name: string; quantity: Quantity; inventoryItemId?: string }[]): { ok: true } | { ok: false; reason: 'storage-full' } }`.
  - **Open store.** The open sessions are kept in a module-level store keyed by case id, not in the state of a component. A session, with its photo, therefore survives a change of route, and a screen that mounts later reads it (GO-BACK).
  - **Older safety rules.** When a record is opened (or arrives by sync) and its `rulesVersion` differs from `SAFETY_RULES_VERSION`, `staleRules` is set and `precheck` runs on the stored description and answers. A hit replaces `outcome` by the escalation. Without a hit the screen shows a notice that the plan was made under older safety rules, before the execution screen, and offers `reassess()`, which sends the case through `assessCase` again and stores the new `rulesVersion` (ARC-002: a changed rule reaches ongoing cases).
  - **Complete.** `complete(used)` does the three things of the completion together: it deducts the used quantities from the inventory, stores `materialsUsed` and sets the status to `completed`. If the storage fails in between, it undoes the deduction and reports `storage-full`, so inventory and record never disagree (UC-015).
  - `start` and `answer` send the description, the photo, every answer so far, the round and `snapshot()` of the inventory; `answer` advances the round from the last questions outcome; questions are returned prefilled by topic (REDUNDANT-ENTRY); a `not sure` answer is kept and the question is not repeated.
  - `chooseOption` requests the explanations of the option's DIY packages; it and `reExplain` send the skill level `levelFor(pkg.area)` with the steps. `reExplain` sets `simpler: true` and `onlyStep: n`.
  - With the user's consent, the photo is saved with `savePhoto` of MOD-history.
- `prefillQuestions(questions: FollowUpQuestion[], answers: Answer[]): FollowUpQuestion[]` — sets `prefill` of every question whose topic an earlier answer covers.

**Errors a caller handles:** a rejected server call, for example offline, resolves as a notice outcome `offline` or `technical-error` and does not throw. A `StorageFullError` from the store is rethrown to the screen, which shows a status message.

## Files

It reads and writes no file directly; the case record goes through MOD-history.

## Uses

- `MOD-case-pipeline.assessCase`, `MOD-case-pipeline.explainSteps` and `MOD-case-pipeline.answerStepQuestion` — the server functions it calls.
- `MOD-history.CaseRecord`, `MOD-history.getCase`, `MOD-history.saveCase`, `MOD-history.savePhoto` and `MOD-history.getPhoto` — loading and saving the case record and its photo.
- `MOD-profile.levelFor` — the level sent with explanations.
- `MOD-hazard-precheck.precheck` and `MOD-case-model.SAFETY_RULES_VERSION` — the re-check of a stored case under newer safety rules.
- `MOD-inventory.deduct` — the deduction on completion.
- `MOD-inventory.snapshot` — the inventory sent with the case.
- `MOD-case-model.CaseOutcome`, `MOD-case-model.Answer`, `MOD-case-model.FollowUpQuestion`, `MOD-case-model.ExplainOutcome`, `MOD-case-model.StepAnswerOutcome`, `MOD-case-model.Money` and `MOD-case-model.Quantity` — the types of its interface.

# MOD-catalogue Sample catalogue and search by spec

## Responsibility

It belongs to Materials and offers (ARC-005). It holds the sample catalogue of new products, second-hand listings and 3D models, and finds the entries that meet the concrete requirements of a needed item.

## Parts

- `index.ts`: the interface.
- The data are not part of this folder: `prototype/data/catalogue/products.json`, `listings.json` and `models.json` (ARC-018).
- `schema.ts`: the zod schemas of the data.
- `spec-match.ts`: the one matcher for products and models. A stated requirement must be met. Dimensions match within ±2 percent, or ±1 mm for values under 50 mm.
- `offers.ts`, `models.ts`, `hints.ts`.
- `*.test.ts`: unit tests. The data files match the schema; every `verified` datum has a source; the search by spec includes matches and excludes misses; second-hand offers come first; models with incomplete data or unreachable links are excluded; nothing is suggested for safety-critical or unclear parts.

## Data

The three JSON files, each entry in the form of `Offer` or `ModelEntry`, every datum in the form of `Datum` (ARC-018).

## Interfaces

- `Certainty` — `'verified' | 'ai-estimate' | 'unverified'`.
- `Datum<T>` — `{ certainty: 'verified'; value: T; source: string } | { certainty: 'ai-estimate' | 'unverified'; value: T | null }`.
- `Offer` — `{ id: string; title: string; condition: 'new' | 'second-hand'; unitPrice: Datum<Money>; packSize: Quantity; spec: { dimensionsMm: Datum<PartSpec['dimensionsMm']>; material: Datum<string>; function: Datum<string> }; compatibility: Datum<'fits'>; availability: Datum<'in-stock' | 'limited' | 'out-of-stock'>; dataAsOf: string; source: { name: string; url: string }; sellerUrl: string; sustainabilityReason: string | null }`.
- `ModelEntry` — `{ id: string; title: string; spec: PartSpec; dimensionsMm: NonNullable<PartSpec['dimensionsMm']>; materialRequirements: string; licence: string; intendedUse: string; url: string; provider: string }`.
- `CATALOGUE_IS_SAMPLE: true` — the whole catalogue is sample data.
- `searchOffers(item: { name: string; spec?: PartSpec }, missing: Quantity): { offers: Offer[]; noMatch: boolean }` — excludes an offer that fails a stated requirement, and treats an `unverified` value as not meeting it; orders all second-hand offers before all new ones, and by unit price within each group; gives `noMatch` when nothing remains.
- `toolHint(need: ToolNeed): string | null` — the rent-or-borrow hint when `need.rentable` is set.
- `searchModels(need: MaterialNeed): Promise<ModelEntry[]>` — an empty list when the part is not printable or `safetyCritical` is not `no`; otherwise the matching models that have complete data and a link that `checkLink` reports reachable.
- `printedPartNote(need: MaterialNeed): string | null` — for a printable part with `safetyCritical` `yes`, the note that a printed part is recommended only together with a professional review.

**Errors a caller handles:** none. `searchModels` never rejects; a failed link check excludes the model.

## Files

# MOD-consent Recorded consents

## Responsibility

It belongs to Personal data (ARC-006). It records which consent the user has given or withdrawn, and starts the removal of data stored under a consent when it is withdrawn.

## Parts

- `index.ts`: the interface.
- `consent.ts`: the records and the purge handlers.
- `*.test.ts`: unit tests. Give, then withdraw, records both; withdrawing runs the purge; giving again works with the same single call; `clearConsents` leaves no key.

## Data

The consent records, stored in localStorage under `daiy.v1.consents`, which is strictly necessary to honour the consents. The plain-language purposes of `CONSENT_PURPOSES`.

## Interfaces

- `ConsentKind` — `'keep-case-photos'`.
- `ConsentRecord` — `{ kind: ConsentKind; given: boolean; at: string }`.
- `CONSENT_PURPOSES: Record<ConsentKind, string>` — the plain-language purpose shown when asking.
- `listConsents(): ConsentRecord[]` — every recorded consent.
- `hasConsent(kind: ConsentKind): boolean` — whether the consent is given now.
- `giveConsent(kind: ConsentKind): void` — one action.
- `withdrawConsent(kind: ConsentKind): Promise<void>` — one action; records the withdrawal, then runs the registered purge handlers.
- `registerPurge(kind: ConsentKind, handler: () => Promise<void>): void` — a handler run on withdrawal.
- `clearConsents(): void` — removes every record.
- `useConsents(): ConsentRecord[]` — the records as a React hook.

**Errors a caller handles:** if a purge handler rejects, `withdrawConsent` passes the rejection on; the withdrawal stays recorded, and nothing more is stored under the consent.

## Files

localStorage key `daiy.v1.consents`, read and written.

## Uses

No other module.

# MOD-cost-estimate Costs and budget

## Responsibility

It belongs to Materials and offers (ARC-005). It computes the estimated total cost of each option, compares it with a stated budget, and lists the prices and fits that still need checking (UC-008 A1 to A4).

## Parts

- `index.ts`: the interface.
- `estimate.ts`: the computation.
- `*.test.ts`: unit tests. The total equals the sum of the item prices; own stock adds nothing; pack rounding; within and exceeding the budget, and no budget; unverified lines are marked.

## Data

It keeps nothing. The rules:

- A line from own stock costs 0.
- A missing or partly available line costs ceil(missing ÷ pack size) × unit price of the chosen offer. The chosen offer defaults to the cheapest from `searchOffers`.
- A line without an offer has `amount` `null` and makes the total `incomplete`.
- `priceToCheck` marks a price that is not `verified`, and `fitToCheck` marks a compatibility that is not `verified`.
- The total is the sum of the line amounts.
- With a budget, each option is `within` or `exceeds`. `noneWithinBudget` is set when no option is within.

## Interfaces

- `CostLine` — `{ name: string; amount: Money | null; fromOwnStock: boolean; priceToCheck: boolean; fitToCheck: boolean }`.
- `OptionCost` — `{ optionId: string; total: Money; incomplete: boolean; lines: CostLine[]; budget: 'within' | 'exceeds' | 'no-budget' }`.
- `estimateCosts(options: { optionId: string; match: StockMatch; chosen: Record<string, Offer | null> }[], budget: Money | null): { costs: OptionCost[]; noneWithinBudget: boolean }` — the costs by the rules under Data.

**Errors a caller handles:** none.

## Files

It reads and writes no file.

- `MOD-catalogue.Offer` and `MOD-catalogue.searchOffers` — the prices, and the default offer.

# MOD-data-portability Export and erase all data

## Responsibility

It belongs to Account, sync and data rights (ARC-007). It writes all of the user's data into one machine-readable file, and erases all of it on the device and in the account.

## Parts

- `index.ts`: the interface.
- `export.ts`, `erase.ts`.
- `*.test.ts`: unit tests. The export contains every section, including empty ones when no data exists; the account section only with an account; erasure leaves no register key and no blob; a failed account deletion is reported.

## Data

The export format is JSON, UTF-8, with the media type `application/json`. Photos are not part of the export, because the user's own photo files remain with the user. The export lists `hadPhoto` per case.

## Interfaces

- `ExportFile` — `{ format: 'daiy-export'; version: 1; exportedAt: string; profile: SkillProfile; materials: MaterialItem[]; tools: ToolItem[]; history: CaseRecord[]; photos: { caseId: string; mime: string; dataBase64: string }[]; consents: ConsentRecord[]; account: AccountData | null }`.
- Kept case photos are part of `ExportFile` (decided by the product owner, 2026-10-27: the user supplied them, so the right to data portability, Art. 20 GDPR, covers them). `exportAll` reads each with `getPhoto` and writes it as base64 in `photos`; there is an entry only for a case whose photo the user chose to keep under the consent `keep-case-photos`.
- `EraseReport` — `{ device: 'erased' | 'failed'; account: 'erased' | 'none' | 'failed'; remaining: string[] }`.
- `ExportError` — `class ExportError extends Error {}`.
- `exportAll(): Promise<Blob>` — the export file; rejects with `ExportError`; stored data stays unchanged.
- `eraseAll(): Promise<EraseReport>` — with an account, `deleteSyncedData`, then `deleteAccount`, where a failure is recorded and the device is erased anyway; when `currentAccount` itself fails (offline), `account` is `'failed'` and `remaining` names the account data on the server; then `localStore.clearAll()`, `clearConsents()` and `resetSync()`; returns the report, whose `remaining` names what could not be erased, for example the account data on the server.

**Errors a caller handles:** `ExportError` from `exportAll`. `eraseAll` does not reject; it reports every failure.

## Files

Through MOD-local-store and MOD-consent, every key of the register and every blob. It produces the export as a download in the browser.

## Uses

- `MOD-profile.getProfile` and `MOD-profile.SkillProfile`, `MOD-inventory.listMaterials`, `MOD-inventory.listTools`, `MOD-inventory.MaterialItem` and `MOD-inventory.ToolItem`, `MOD-history.listCases`, `MOD-history.CaseRecord` and `MOD-history.getPhoto`, `MOD-consent.listConsents` and `MOD-consent.ConsentRecord` — the sections of the export.
- `MOD-consent.clearConsents` and `MOD-local-store.localStore` — erasure on the device.
- `MOD-accounts.currentAccount`, `MOD-accounts.deleteAccount` and `MOD-accounts.AccountData` — the account section and the account's deletion.
- `MOD-sync-store.deleteSyncedData` — the synced copy's deletion.
- `MOD-sync-client.resetSync` — the sync marks after erasure.

## Responsibility

It belongs to the User interface (ARC-008). It presents the user's own data and rights: profile, inventory, history, consents, privacy notice, export, erasure and account.

## Parts

- `index.ts`: the interface.
- `ProfileScreen`: the areas with a simple level scale, the stored level shown, and areas left open shown as beginner.
- `InventoryScreen`: add, change and remove materials and tools, with errors that name the field.
- `HistoryScreen`: ongoing and completed cases, each opened with its steps, materials used and editable notes, and an empty state. The notes are the only part of a record that the user edits (UC-021); a wrong entry under materials used is corrected in the inventory, not in the record.
- `PrivacyScreen`: the full `PrivacyNotice`; consents with a one-action toggle each, giving and withdrawing alike; export as a download; delete all data with a warning, an export offer and confirmation, followed by the report.
- `AccountScreen`: the `PrivacyNotice` before the sign-up form; sign up and sign in with paste-enabled password fields; passkey add and sign-in through `@simplewebauthn/browser`; change user name or password, and sign out; the sync state.
- `PrivacyNotice`: the text with six items (PRIVACY-NOTICE): the controller's identity and contact; the purposes and legal bases (case answers, account and sync); the recipients (hosting provider and AI provider, with the transfer to a third country, ARC-010); the storage periods, including the 30 days of backups (ARC-012); the user's rights; and the right to complain to a supervisory authority. # MOD-hazard-precheck Hazard catalogue and pre-check

## Responsibility

It belongs to the Case domain (ARC-002). It recognises hazard and out-of-scope signals in text written in English and German, and builds the escalation that fits the detected kinds.

## Parts

- `index.ts`: the interface.
- `catalogue.ts`: one entry per `HazardKind`. Each entry holds:
  - whether the kind is an emergency;
  - its English and German patterns;
  - its immediate actions;
  - the kind of professional to contact;
  - the reason why no instructions are given.
- `precheck.ts`: the detection and the escalation builder.
- `*.test.ts`: unit tests, one per kind, and one for `opensHousing` with an English and a German positive and a near-miss negative: an English and a German positive, a near-miss negative, and the inputs of the classification cases, which are not blocked. The subsystem test `src/test/safety.test.ts` covers the checks the SPEC names: the actions and the professional of each kind; `high` for out-of-scope work and `critical` for an emergency; emergency actions first for a mixed input.

## Data

The catalogue lists two groups of kinds:

- **Emergencies:** gas, carbon monoxide, fire or smoke, overheating or scorched electrics, water near electrics, structural damage.
- **Out of scope:** distribution board, fixed 230/400 V installation, grid connection, gas installation, refrigerant circuit, load-bearing structure, chimney, energy renovation.

The patterns do not match installation work that can be one package of a larger project: a new socket, a ceiling light or a wallbox (PRECHECK-SPARES-PROJECT-PACKAGES). Each kind's actions belong only to that kind (HAZARD-SAFETY-MEASURES). For example, a carbon monoxide alarm gets ventilation, leaving the room and calling the emergency number, and never advice on the fuse box. No action presents a fuse-box switch-off as securing a circuit (NO-BREAKER-ONLY-ISOLATION).

## Interfaces

- `detectHazards(text: string): HazardKind[]` — the detected kinds in catalogue order, without duplicates.
- `precheck(texts: string[]): Escalation | null` — joins all texts, which are the description and every follow-up answer or the step question, and returns `null` when no kind is detected. Otherwise it returns `escalationFor(kinds, 'precheck')`.
- `opensHousing(text: string): boolean` — whether a step text tells the reader to open a mains housing: a distribution board, a fuse box or consumer unit, or the housing of a mains-powered device or its power supply, with English and German patterns kept in the catalogue (`catalogue.ts`). Enforcement uses it as a second line behind the AI's own `opensMainsHousing` flag.
- `escalationFor(kinds: HazardKind[], origin: 'precheck' | 'output'): Escalation` — builds the escalation:
  - `risk` is `critical` if any kind is an emergency, and `high` otherwise;
  - `actions` and `professionals` list the emergency kinds before the others, without duplicates;
  - `reason` is a plain-language sentence that names the kinds and says why no instructions are given;
  - an empty `kinds` list gives the generic escalation: stop the work, and contact a qualified professional of the trade concerned.

**Errors a caller handles:** none. The functions are total.

## Files

It reads and writes no file.

## Uses

- `MOD-case-model.HazardKind` and `MOD-case-model.Escalation` — the kinds it detects and the escalation it builds.

# MOD-inventory Material and tool inventory

## Responsibility

It belongs to Personal data (ARC-006). It stores the materials and tools the user owns, validates new entries and deducts consumed quantities.

## Parts

- `index.ts`: the interface.
- `materials.ts`, `tools.ts`, `validate.ts`.
- `*.test.ts`: unit tests. Save with and without a location; each missing field is named; change and remove; `deduct` with more than held clamps to 0; `snapshot`; the data persists across reload.

## Data

Materials in the collection `materials` and tools in the collection `tools` of MOD-local-store. Validation: `name` must be non-empty; `amount` must be a number ≥ 0; `unit` must be one of the units of MOD-case-model; `location` is optional. Each error names its field.

## Interfaces

- `MaterialItem` — `{ id: string; name: string; quantity: Quantity; location?: string }`.
- `ToolItem` — `{ id: string; name: string }`.
- `MaterialInput` — `{ name: string; amount: number | null; unit: Unit | null; location?: string }`.
- `InventoryFieldError` — `{ field: 'name' | 'amount' | 'unit'; message: string }`.
- `listMaterials(): MaterialItem[]` — every material.
- `saveMaterial(input: MaterialInput, id?: string): { ok: true; item: MaterialItem } | { ok: false; errors: InventoryFieldError[] }` — adds or changes a material.
- `removeMaterial(id: string): void` — removes a material.
- `listTools(): ToolItem[]` — every tool.
- `saveTool(name: string, id?: string): { ok: true; item: ToolItem } | { ok: false; errors: InventoryFieldError[] }` — adds or changes a tool.

# MOD-local-store Repository on the device

## Responsibility

It belongs to Personal data (ARC-006). It stores the user's records and blobs on the device, and keeps the register that names, for every stored item, the basis on which it is stored.

## Parts

- `index.ts`: the interface.
- `records.ts`: localStorage collections.
- `blobs.ts`: IndexedDB through `idb-keyval`.
- `register.ts`: the storage register.
- `events.ts`: change subscription.
- `*.test.ts`: unit tests with jsdom and fake-indexeddb. The records persist; tombstones; `changedSince`; `applyRemote`, newest wins; a blob is refused without consent and purged on withdrawal; `clearAll` leaves no register key; every key the app writes is in the register.

## Data

The register `STORAGE_REGISTER` lists every key:

| Key | Basis |
|---|---|
| `daiy.v1.profile` | necessary for the skill profile |
| `daiy.v1.materials` | necessary for the inventory |
| `daiy.v1.tools` | necessary for the inventory |
| `daiy.v1.cases` | necessary for the project history |
| `daiy.v1.consents` | necessary to record consents (MOD-consent) |
| `daiy.v1.sync` | necessary for the sync the user started (MOD-sync-client) |
| `case-photo` blobs | consent `keep-case-photos` |
| cookie `daiy_session` (set by the server, ARC-013) | necessary for the sign-in the user requested |

At start, the module registers `removeBlobs('case-photo')` as the purge handler of `keep-case-photos` with MOD-consent.

## Interfaces

- `Collection` — `'profile' | 'materials' | 'tools' | 'cases'`.
- `BlobKind` — `'case-photo'`.
- `StoredRecord<T>` — `{ id: string; collection: Collection; updatedAt: number; deleted: boolean; data: T }`.
- `StorageBasis` — `{ kind: 'necessary'; for: string } | { kind: 'consent'; consent: ConsentKind }`.
- `StorageFullError` — `class StorageFullError extends Error {}`, thrown when localStorage is full.
- `ConsentMissingError` — `class ConsentMissingError extends Error { readonly consent: ConsentKind }`, thrown when a blob is written without its consent.
- `STORAGE_REGISTER: Record<string, StorageBasis>` — the register under Data.
- `localStore` — the repository object:
  - `list<T>(c: Collection): StoredRecord<T>[]` — without tombstones;
  - `get<T>(c: Collection, id: string): StoredRecord<T> | undefined`;
  - `put<T>(c: Collection, id: string, data: T): StoredRecord<T>` — sets `updatedAt = Date.now()`; throws `StorageFullError`;
  - `remove(c: Collection, id: string): void` — writes a tombstone;
  - `changedSince(ts: number): StoredRecord<unknown>[]` — with tombstones, for sync;
  - `applyRemote(records: StoredRecord<unknown>[]): void` — keeps the later `updatedAt`; ties keep the local copy;
  - `subscribe(listener: (c: Collection) => void): () => void`;
  - `putBlob(kind: BlobKind, id: string, blob: Blob): Promise<void>` — rejects with `ConsentMissingError`;
  - `getBlob(kind: BlobKind, id: string): Promise<Blob | undefined>`;
  - `removeBlobs(kind: BlobKind): Promise<void>`;
  - `clearAll(): Promise<void>` — every key of the register and every blob.

**Errors a caller handles:** `StorageFullError` and `ConsentMissingError`.

## Files

- localStorage keys `daiy.v1.profile`, `daiy.v1.materials`, `daiy.v1.tools` and `daiy.v1.cases`, read and written; `clearAll` also removes the other keys of the register.
- IndexedDB database `keyval-store`, read and written.

## Uses

- `MOD-consent.ConsentKind` — the basis of consent-gated items.
- `MOD-consent.hasConsent` — before writing a blob.
- `MOD-consent.registerPurge` — to purge photos when their consent is withdrawn.

# MOD-output-check Accept or reject an AI draft

## Responsibility

It belongs to the Case domain (ARC-002). It decides whether an unvalidated AI output may go on. It checks the expected format, completeness and prohibited paths, and returns either the typed draft or the list of failures. Risk is not judged here; MOD-safety-enforcement converts high risk.

## Parts

- `index.ts`: the interface.
- `format.ts`: schema parse with the schemas of MOD-case-model.
- `completeness.ts`: the completeness rules listed under Interfaces.
- `prohibited.ts`: path rules and the prohibited-claim patterns in English and German.
- `check.ts`: the three public functions.
- `*.test.ts`: unit tests. One malformed, one incomplete and one prohibited draft per rule, each caught; one valid draft per kind, accepted; the prohibited-claim patterns in English and German, with near-miss negatives.

## Data

The prohibited-claim patterns are a closed table in `prohibited.ts`, each with an English and a German pattern; a new pattern is a new row, not a new function:

| Pattern | Requirement |
|---|---|
| the circuit breaker alone secures a circuit against being switched on again | NO-BREAKER-ONLY-ISOLATION |
| a permit-free project is free of other rules | PERMIT-FREE-NOT-RULE-FREE |
| a CO₂ figure in a sustainability statement, unless it carries a source | SUSTAINABILITY-EXPLAINED |
| a step, a warning or a safety measure may be skipped, left out or shortened, for example by experience ("experienced users can skip …") | SKILL-DOES-NOT-UNLOCK |
| there is no need to switch off, unplug or isolate | UNPLUG-BEFORE-OPENING, NO-BREAKER-ONLY-ISOLATION |
| opening a distribution board, a fuse box or a mains housing is described as a DIY action | NO-OPENING-MAINS-HOUSINGS |

`basics` have a maximum length of 600 characters, a chosen value that no requirement fixes.

## Interfaces

- `CheckFailure` — `{ check: 'format' | 'completeness' | 'prohibited-path'; path: string; message: string }`.
- `CheckResult<T>` — `{ ok: true; value: T } | { ok: false; failures: CheckFailure[] }`.
- `checkAssessmentDraft(raw: unknown, ctx: { round: 0 | 1 | 2 }): CheckResult<AssessmentDraft>` — its rules:
  - **Format:** the draft matches `schemas.assessmentDraft`.
  - **Completeness, for kind `questions`:** `missing` is non-empty and at least one question has text.
  - **Completeness, for kind `answer`:** `summary` is non-empty and at least one option exists; every package has a title, an area, a label, a reason and a handover brief; a package with `labelUncertain` has non-empty `decidingInformation`; every `diy` or `diy-preparation` package has a guide with a diagnosis, tools and materials lists, steps numbered 1..n without gaps, a time range and at least one warning.
  - **Prohibited paths:** questions at round 2; a guide in a package that the draft itself labels `professional-only` or `not-recommended`; an image id unknown to MOD-illustrations; any text that matches a prohibited-claim pattern.
- `checkExplanationDraft(raw: unknown, req: ExplainRequest): CheckResult<ExplanationDraft>` — exactly one non-empty `basics` per requested step, only for requested step numbers; no `basics` longer than 600 characters; no text that matches a prohibited-claim pattern, in particular none that skips, relaxes or replaces a step or a warning.
- `checkStepAnswerDraft(raw: unknown): CheckResult<StepAnswerDraft>` — the format matches; the answer is non-empty; no text matches a prohibited-claim pattern; `detectHazards` finds no hazard kind in the answer (a hit is a `prohibited-path` failure, and the pipeline then answers with the generic notice or, when the draft's `risk` is high, with the escalation).

**Errors a caller handles:** none thrown. Every failure is returned in `failures`.

## Files

It reads and writes no file.

## Uses

- `MOD-case-model.schemas` — the format check.
- `MOD-case-model.AssessmentDraft`, `MOD-case-model.ExplanationDraft`, `MOD-case-model.ExplainRequest` and `MOD-case-model.StepAnswerDraft` — the types it checks and returns.
- `MOD-illustrations.illustration` — to reject image ids that are not in the catalogue.
- `MOD-hazard-precheck.detectHazards` — the hazard check of a step answer.

# MOD-safety-enforcement Shape a checked draft by the safety rules

## Responsibility

It belongs to the Case domain (ARC-002). It turns an accepted AI draft into the outcome that the safety rules allow: escalation, follow-up questions or guidance with enforced labels and fixed safety steps. No rule reads a skill level; the module has none to read (ARC-011).

## Parts

- `index.ts`: the interface.
- `enforce.ts`: the rules, applied in order.
- `fixed.ts`: the fixed texts: the questions for model, variant, load and dimensions; the shut-off-water step; the unplug step; the lock-out warning against switching on again; the advice to agree preparation with the professional beforehand; the note on unknown models.
- `*.test.ts`: unit tests per rule, including the order of rules and the "not sure" answer to the load and dimension questions in rule 4. The subsystem test `src/test/safety.test.ts` covers the SPEC's check: a guide with high risk becomes an escalation without a guide.

## Data

The fixed texts only.

## Interfaces

- `EnforceContext` — `{ round: 0 | 1 | 2; answers: Answer[] }`.
- `enforceSafety(draft: AssessmentDraft, ctx: EnforceContext): CaseOutcome` — never of type `notice`; guidance is returned with notices empty and options unranked. Its rules, in order; the first rule that yields an escalation ends the run, and questions are collected across rules:
  1. **Escalation.** `outOfScope` is set, or `risk` is `high` or `critical`: return `escalationFor(hazards plus outOfScope, 'output')`. The result has no guide (NO-GUIDE-AT-HIGH-RISK).
  1b. **Hazards in the output text.** `detectHazards` runs over the `summary`, the `photoDescription`, every package title and reason and every step text of the draft. Any hit gives `escalationFor(kinds, 'output')`, as in rule 1, whatever `risk` says. This is a deterministic second line behind the flags the AI sets itself: a socket described harmlessly but scorched in the photo, or a guide with `risk: low` whose steps open a distribution board, no longer reaches the user as a DIY guide (RISK-CHECK-FIRST, NO-GUIDE-AT-HIGH-RISK).
  2. **Unclear risk.** `riskUncertain` is set. Before round 2, return the draft's questions, or an escalation if it has none. At round 2, return an escalation (UNCLEAR-CASES-CONSERVATIVE).
  3. **Device model.** The case concerns a device and the model is unknown. Before round 2, put the model and variant questions first and name no part. At round 2, remove the replacement-part materials and add the unknown-model assumption (MODEL-BEFORE-PARTS).
  4. **Person-carrying furniture.** A package carries a person, and the load is missing, or the dimensions are missing. A value is missing when no answer has that topic, or when the answer has `notSure: true`; a "not sure" is therefore not an answer here. Before round 2, add the load and dimension questions. At round 2, set the label to `not-recommended` with load and dimensions as deciding information.
  5. **Questions.** If the draft kind is `questions`, or rules 3 or 4 added questions, and the round is below 2, return the questions with round = ctx.round + 1.
  6. **Mains housing.** A package with `opensMainsHousing`, or with a step text for which `opensHousing` is true (rule 6b, again a second line behind the flag), gets the label `professional-only` (NO-OPENING-MAINS-HOUSINGS).
  7. **Uncertain label.** A package with `labelUncertain` gets `stricterLabel(label, alternativeLabel or the next stricter label)` (STRICTER-LABEL-IF-UNCERTAIN).
  8. **Guide removal.** A package labelled `professional-only` or `not-recommended` loses its guide.
  9. **Preparation.** A `diy-preparation` package gets the agree-beforehand text.
  10. **Fixed safety steps**, in each remaining guide: water-related work starts with the shut-off step; the unplug step comes before the first step that opens a device; a guide with a step that switches off a circuit gets the lock-out warning; the steps are renumbered.
  11. **Unclear safety-critical status.** A material with `safetyCritical` `unclear` becomes `yes`.
  12. **Result.** Return guidance with the draft's summary, assumptions and `photoDescription` as `photoAlt`.
- `enforceStepAnswer(draft: StepAnswerDraft): StepAnswerOutcome` — `risk` `high` or `critical` gives `escalationFor(hazards, 'output')`; so does any hazard kind that `detectHazards` finds in the answer text; otherwise the answer is returned.

**Errors a caller handles:** none. The functions are total over valid drafts.

## Files

It reads and writes no file.

## Uses

- `MOD-case-model.AssessmentDraft`, `MOD-case-model.Answer`, `MOD-case-model.CaseOutcome`, `MOD-case-model.StepAnswerDraft` and `MOD-case-model.StepAnswerOutcome` — what it receives and returns.
- `MOD-case-model.stricterLabel` — rule 7.
- `MOD-case-model.FIXED_TOPICS` — the topics of the fixed questions and of the answers it looks for.
- `MOD-hazard-precheck.escalationFor` — the escalations of rules 1, 1b and 2 and of `enforceStepAnswer`.
- `MOD-hazard-precheck.detectHazards` and `MOD-hazard-precheck.opensHousing` — rules 1b and 6.

# MOD-stock-matching Materials and tools against the inventory

## Responsibility

It belongs to Materials and offers (ARC-005). It derives the bill of materials and the tool list of an option from its guides, and matches them against the inventory.

## Parts

- `index.ts`: the interface.
- `bill.ts`: aggregates the same material across the packages of an option.
- `units.ts`: conversion within length (mm, cm, m), volume (ml, l) and mass (g, kg). Area and pieces are not converted.
- `match.ts`: the matching.
- `*.test.ts`: unit tests. Quantities below, equal to and above the requirement; unit conversion, and an incompatible unit; aggregation across packages; missing tools apart; an empty inventory.

## Data

It keeps nothing. The matching rules:

- Names match after trimming and case folding.
- A held quantity in a compatible unit is converted. held ≥ required gives `available`; 0 < held < required gives `partly-available` with `missing` = required − held; otherwise, including an incompatible unit, `missing` with the full quantity.
- `materials` lists available items first, then partly available, then missing (OWN-STOCK-FIRST).
- Tools are split into owned and missing.
- An empty guide list gives empty lists.

## Interfaces

- `StockStatus` — `{ kind: 'available' } | { kind: 'partly-available'; missing: Quantity } | { kind: 'missing'; missing: Quantity }`.
- `MaterialMatch` — `{ need: MaterialNeed; inventoryItemId: string | null; held: Quantity | null; status: StockStatus }`.
- `ToolMatch` — `{ need: ToolNeed; inventoryToolId: string | null }`.
- `StockMatch` — `{ materials: MaterialMatch[]; ownedTools: ToolMatch[]; missingTools: ToolMatch[] }`.
- `matchStock(guides: Guide[], inventory: { materials: MaterialItem[]; tools: ToolItem[] }): StockMatch` — the match by the rules under Data.

**Errors a caller handles:** none. The function is total.

## Files

It reads and writes no file.

## Uses

- `MOD-case-model.Guide`, `MOD-case-model.MaterialNeed`, `MOD-case-model.ToolNeed`, `MOD-case-model.Quantity` and `MOD-case-model.Unit` — the needs and quantities it matches.
- `MOD-inventory.MaterialItem` and `MOD-inventory.ToolItem` — the inventory items it matches against.

# MOD-sync-client Keep device and account equal

## Responsibility

It belongs to Account, sync and data rights (ARC-007). It pushes local changes to the account, and pulls and applies remote changes, whenever the user is signed in (UC-018 A3 and A4).

## Parts

- `index.ts`: the interface.
- `sync.ts`: the triggers and the sync step.
- `*.test.ts`: unit tests with the server functions replaced. An offline change is pushed later; a remote change is applied; newest wins on conflict; nothing happens without an account.

## Data

The localStorage key `daiy.v1.sync` holds `{ lastPushedAt: number; cursor: number; accountId: string }`. A sync step:

1. Check for an account with `currentAccount`. Without one, do nothing.
2. `push(localStore.changedSince(lastPushedAt))`.
3. `pull({since: cursor})`, then `localStore.applyRemote`.
4. Update the marks.

## Interfaces

- `SyncState` — `{ signedIn: boolean; status: 'idle' | 'syncing' | 'offline' | 'error' | 'account-changed'; lastSyncedAt: number | null }`, shown as a status message.
- `startSync(): () => void` — starts the triggers: app start, local change (2 s debounce), online event; returns a stop function.
- `syncNow(): Promise<SyncState>` — one sync step on demand.
- `resetSync(): void` — removes the marks, after sign-out or delete-all.
- `resolveAccountChange(choice: 'merge' | 'clear'): Promise<SyncState>` — after a sign-in as an account other than the one in the mark: `merge` pushes the device records to the new account, `clear` empties the device collections first. Until it is called, the status is `account-changed` and nothing is pushed.
- `useSyncState(): SyncState` — the state as a React hook.

**Errors a caller handles:** none thrown. A network failure sets `offline` and keeps the marks, so the changes are pushed later; HTTP 401 sets `signedIn` to false; a rejected record sets `error`.

## Files

The localStorage key `daiy.v1.sync`, read and written.

## Uses

- `MOD-local-store.localStore` — `changedSince`, `applyRemote` and `subscribe`.
- `MOD-sync-store.push` and `MOD-sync-store.pull` — the server side of sync.
- `MOD-accounts.currentAccount` — whether a user is signed in.

# MOD-sync-store Synced copy on the server

## Responsibility

It belongs to Account, sync and data rights (ARC-007). It keeps the synced copy of the records of each account and gives it to that account's devices.

## Parts

- `index.ts`: the interface.
- `db.ts`: the connection to `data/sync.sqlite` and the migrations.
- `functions.ts`: the server functions.
- `*.test.ts`: unit tests. Newer wins, and ties keep the stored copy; `pull` after a cursor; isolation between accounts; tombstones are passed on; a record that is too large is rejected; delete removes all of the account's rows.

## Data

The table `records(account_id, collection, id, updated_at, deleted, data_json, seq)`, keyed by `(account_id, collection, id)`. The column `seq` is a growing sequence number.

## Interfaces

Server functions, called remotely from the browser over HTTPS POST. Each serves only the account of the session. On the client, a network failure rejects the promise.

- `push: (i: { records: StoredRecord<unknown>[] }) => Promise<{ accepted: number; rejected: { id: string; reason: 'too-large' }[] }>` — stores a record if no copy exists or its `updatedAt` is later (ARC-014). A record larger than 256 KB is rejected.
- `pull: (i: { since: number }) => Promise<{ records: StoredRecord<unknown>[]; cursor: number }>` — the account's records with `seq` greater than `since`.
- `deleteSyncedData: () => Promise<{ ok: true }>` — removes all of the account's rows.

**Errors a caller handles:** `UnauthenticatedError` reaches the client as HTTP 401 without a session.

## Files

`data/sync.sqlite`, read and written.

## Uses

- `MOD-accounts.requireAccountId` and `MOD-accounts.UnauthenticatedError` — the account of the session.
- `MOD-local-store.StoredRecord` — the form of a synced record. It is imported with `import type` only, which leaves nothing of the client module in the server build. It uses the library `better-sqlite3`.

# MOD-ui-kit Accessible building blocks

## Responsibility

It belongs to the User interface (ARC-008). It provides the components and design tokens from which every screen is built, so that the accessibility requirements hold by construction.

## Parts

- `index.ts`: the interface.
- `tokens.css`: Tailwind theme with text colours at 4.5:1 or more against their backgrounds, and 3:1 for large text; borders and state indicators at 3:1 against adjacent colours; a focus ring of 2 px with 3:1 contrast; sizes in rem, so text scales to 200 percent.
- `components/`: the shadcn components that are used, wrapped.
- `announcer.tsx`: one polite live region.
- `*.test.tsx`: Testing Library tests of names and labels, the link between an error and its field, `announce` writing to the live region without moving focus, and a collapsible operable by keyboard; a token test computes the contrast ratios of all token pairs.

## Data

None.

## Interfaces

- `IconName` — the names of the lucide icons the app uses.
- `Button(p: { label: string; icon?: IconName; variant?: 'primary' | 'secondary' | 'danger'; onPress: () => void; disabled?: boolean }): JSX.Element` — a target of at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels.
- `IconButton(p: { label: string; icon: IconName; onPress: () => void }): JSX.Element` — the label is required and is the accessible name.
- `LinkButton(p: { label: string; href: string; external?: boolean }): JSX.Element` — an external link opens in a new tab with `rel=noopener` and says so in text.
- `TextField(p: { label: string; value: string; onChange: (v: string) => void; error?: string; multiline?: boolean; autoComplete?: string; type?: 'text' | 'password' | 'number' }): JSX.Element` — the error is linked by `aria-describedby` and `aria-invalid`; paste is allowed.
- `Select<T extends string>(p: { label: string; value: T | null; options: { value: T; label: string }[]; onChange: (v: T) => void; error?: string }): JSX.Element` — a labelled choice.
- `Checkbox(p: { label: string; checked: boolean; onChange: (v: boolean) => void }): JSX.Element` — a labelled check box.
- `Collapsible(p: { summary: string; defaultOpen: boolean; children: ReactNode }): JSX.Element` — operable by keyboard.
- `StatusBadge(p: { tone: 'ok' | 'warning' | 'danger' | 'info'; icon: IconName; text: string }): JSX.Element` — text always present, never colour alone.
- `Img(p: { src: string; alt: string } | { src: string; decorative: true }): JSX.Element` — an image with a text alternative, or marked decorative.
- `Dialog(p: { title: string; open: boolean; onClose: () => void; children: ReactNode }): JSX.Element` — a titled dialog.
- `Page(p: { title: string; back?: { label: string; onBack: () => void }; children: ReactNode }): JSX.Element` — single column, no horizontal scroll at 320 CSS pixels, with the back action.
- `announce(message: string): void` — a status message without a change of focus.

**Errors a caller handles:** none.

## Files

It reads and writes no file.

## Uses

No DAIY module. It uses React, Radix through shadcn/ui, Tailwind, sonner and lucide-react.
